- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!

```

re-read changed files,

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```

  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)

- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

- **PR #**: 1069

- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed

```

With result-bytes dedupe, repeats attach only when clipboard content unchanged → also suppressed! Current design: two deliberate ctrl+v of the same image within 500ms → second suppressed. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. - **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

For a big text paste chunked into N messages, N osascript/PowerShell spawns. On Windows PowerShell spawn ~1-2s CPU each — noticeable but bounded by chunk count. Worth a SUGGESTION (perf): gate the probe to empty-content pastes or rate-limit. Hmm — but would gating to empty-content break the AC2 "text paste attaches image"? The PR deliberately supports attaching image alongside text (AC2). Terminal behavior: when you paste with an image in the clipboard, most terminals deliver an empty bracketed paste; but AC2's scenario (text AND image) happens when the terminal inserts a file path for the image + user pastes text? Not sure of real-world flow; the PR explicitly claims AC2. I'll keep the perf note as a SUGGESTION without proposing gating that breaks AC2.

Let me think again about the probe ordering: In the TUI runtime, when the user presses ctrl+v in a bracketed-paste terminal, the terminal sends the key event AND the bracketed paste sequence. Both arrive as separate input events. The model fires a Cmd for each; Cmds typically run concurrently (each is an async function). Results dispatched as messages. Since both subprocesses are spawned within ms, they usually complete within ms of each other. To exceed the 500ms window, one read must stall 500ms+ relative to the other. Possible on Windows (PowerShell startup contention) or macOS first-run permission dialogs! Actually notable: on macOS, the FIRST osascript clipboard read triggers a TCC permission prompt (System Events → "Terminal wants to paste"). While the permission dialog is open, reads hang for SECONDS. Both probes would hang together though... they'd both resolve after approval within ms of each other. The skew case is one probe queued while the other runs (osascript spawns serialize?). osascript spawns don't serialize. Low probability. And vice versa: if a PasteMsg fired a probe, a following ctrl+v within the window skips. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? - **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence

  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)

dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

Let me now run the other regression test files mentioned in the PR to confirm, then check a couple of remaining review angles:

1. How does the runtime dispatch Cmds — concurrently or sequentially? For the dedupe race analysis. Let me peek at dart_tui's runtime. Not critical.

2. Check `_withFreshCtrlCWindow` — does it do anything with the returned model that might drop fields? It wraps handler; returns result. Fine.

6. Consider: `_handlePaste` fires probe for EVERY PasteMsg — including PasteMsg delivered while busy (stream deltas during an active run?) — pastes while the agent is busy: the composer still accepts input (steering). Probe fires → subprocess spawn mid-run. Fine, same as typing.

7. Multi-chunk bracketed pastes (tmux splitting) → multiple PasteMsg → multiple probes → multiple concurrent subprocess spawns. Each silently fails or succeeds. For a big text paste chunked into N messages, N osascript/PowerShell spawns. On Windows PowerShell spawn ~1-2s CPU each — noticeable but bounded by chunk count. Worth a SUGGESTION (perf): gate the probe to empty-content pastes or rate-limit. Hmm — but would gating to empty-content break the AC2 "text paste attaches image"? The PR deliberately supports attaching image alongside text (AC2). Terminal behavior: when you paste with an image in the clipboard, most terminals deliver an empty bracketed paste; but AC2's scenario (text AND image) happens when the terminal inserts a file path for the image + user pastes text? Not sure of real-world flow; the PR explicitly claims AC2. I'll keep the perf note as a SUGGESTION without proposing gating that breaks AC2.

8. The `_bytesEqual` — package:collection not in pubspec (grep found nothing), so hand-rolled is justified. Could use `ListEquality` if collection were a dep — skip.

9. Missing test: oversized image via bracketed paste stays silent (the `pasteImageError` + silentFailure path). Also missing: bracketed-paste probe result that is `PasteboardImage` with garbage bytes → silent. One test would cover both (garbage bytes → pasteImageError → silent). SUGGESTION.

10. Memory retention: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` keeps referencing the byte list after attachments are cleared on submit — retains up to maxPasteImageBytes (check cap value) until next image attach. Let me check maxPasteImageBytes value. Small note → SUGGESTION.

11. Dedupe window vs slow reads (analyzed above) — SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. Let me think again about the probe ordering: In the TUI runtime, when the user presses ctrl+v in a bracketed-paste terminal, the terminal sends the key event AND the bracketed paste sequence. Both arrive as separate input events. The model fires a Cmd for each; Cmds typically run concurrently (each is an async function). Results dispatched as messages. Since both subprocesses are spawned within ms, they usually complete within ms of each other. To exceed the 500ms window, one read must stall 500ms+ relative to the other. Possible on Windows (PowerShell startup contention) or macOS first-run permission dialogs! Actually notable: on macOS, the FIRST osascript clipboard read triggers a TCC permission prompt (System Events → "Terminal wants to paste"). While the permission dialog is open, reads hang for SECONDS. Both probes would hang together though... they'd both resolve after approval within ms of each other. The skew case is one probe queued while the other runs (osascript spawns serialize?). osascript spawns don't serialize. Low probability. I'll file as SUGGESTION with the alternative design note (gesture-level dedupe: mark that a paste gesture already has an in-flight probe and let the second event of the same gesture skip its probe; or widen to sequence-based pairing). Actually a cleaner gesture-level approach: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires a probe, stamp `_pendingProbeAtMs = now`; `_handlePaste` skips its probe if `now - _pendingProbeAtMs < window`. And vice versa: if a PasteMsg fired a probe, a following ctrl+v within the window skips. This halves spawns AND removes the bytes comparison and the identical-bytes requirement (handles the case where the clipboard CHANGED between the two reads of one gesture — currently that attaches two different images... wait if clipboard changed between the two reads, the user copied something else within ms — pathological; gesture-level dedupe handles it more correctly too).

With result-bytes dedupe, repeats attach only when clipboard content unchanged → also suppressed! Current design: two deliberate ctrl+v of the same image within 500ms → second suppressed. Both designs trade off. The chosen design is reasonable; I'll note the residual race only.

So an oversized image: first ctrl+v → named error printed, NOT recorded in dedupe state (returns early). Bracketed probe → silent return. No dedupe interplay. Good — errors don't poison the dedupe state.

15. `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` updated on `next` — the returned model. But the mid-flight second probe result handled against the model state that HAS the field copied. Good.

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```

  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)

  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!

  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)

```

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI file-size gate will fail — `fa_tui.dart` is now 2817 lines (limit 2800)**

`AGENTS.md` ("Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file"), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)", `exit 1` on violation) and `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` (`MAX_LINES=2800`) all enforce this. `origin/main` sits at **exactly 2800**; this PR adds 17 net lines → **2817**. lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart: 2817 lines   # → CI exits 1
```

The `fa_tui_paste.dart` header itself documents the gate ("split out of `fa_tui.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate").

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

`read.bytes` (≤ `maxPasteboardImageBytes` = 10 MB) stays referenced by the dedupe state even after a submit consumes the attachments, and is never cleared — the memory is retained until the *next* image attach. Two cheap options:

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.

💡 **SUGGESTION: one clipboard-reader subprocess per bracketed-paste message**

Every `PasteMsg` now spawns the platform reader (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell — PowerShell startup alone is ~100s of ms). Most terminals deliver a paste as one bracketed sequence, but some (tmux/screen under buffer limits) split large pastes into **multiple** bracketed-paste blocks — a single big log paste then fires N subprocess spawns, each silently failing or reading an unrelated clipboard image. Bounded by user actions, so low risk, but a small rate-limit (e.g. skip the probe if one fired <200 ms ago, share the injectable `nowFn`) would cap the fan-out without changing any tested behavior.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1069
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1069
- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

re-read changed files,

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!

`AGENTS.md` ("Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file"), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)", `exit 1` on violation) and `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` (`MAX_LINES=2800`) all enforce this. `origin/main` sits at **exactly 2800**; this PR adds 17 net lines → **2817**. The `fa_tui_paste.dart` header itself documents the gate ("split out of `fa_tui.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate").

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.
