Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. ## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)

```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1069
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1069
- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +291
- **Deletions**: -41
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T22:54:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the silent `pasteImageError` branch is untested, and total silence on an image-paste gesture is questionable UX**

This `silentFailure` early-return for *image bytes that fail validation* (oversized > 10 MB, or unrecognized magic) is the only silent-failure branch with no test — the new suite only covers `PasteboardUnavailable`. One test pins the invariant end-to-end:

```dart
test('an oversized clipboard image on a bracketed paste stays silent', () async {
  var model = build(
    reader: () async => PasteboardImage(List.filled(maxPasteImageBytes + 1, 0)),
    inputText: '',
  );
  final (next, cmd) = model.update(PasteMsg(''));
  model = next as FaTuiModel;
  final followUp = await cmd?.call();
  model = model.update(followUp!).$1 as FaTuiModel;
  expect(model.attachments, isEmpty);
  expect(model.outputLines, isEmpty); // silent, per the issue invariant

When that image is over the cap, Ctrl+V names the failure ("clipboard image too large … downscale") but menu-Paste/Cmd+V gives *zero* feedback, indistinguishable from a dead key. Consider naming the failure only when `msg.content` was empty (clear image intent), keeping text pastes fully silent as AC requires.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

  var model = build(
    reader: () async => PasteboardImage(List.filled(maxPasteImageBytes + 1, 0)),
    inputText: '',

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).

`AGENTS.md` ("Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file"), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)", `exit 1` on violation) and `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` (`MAX_LINES=2800`) all enforce this. `origin/main` sits at **exactly 2800**; this PR adds 17 net lines → **2817**. The `fa_tui_paste.dart` header itself documents the gate ("split out of `fa_tui.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate").

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

`read.bytes` (≤ `maxPasteboardImageBytes` = 10 MB) stays referenced by the dedupe state even after a submit consumes the attachments, and is never cleared — the memory is retained until the *next* image attach. Two cheap options:

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. ## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```

  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)

The `fa_tui_paste.dart` header itself documents the gate ("split out of `fa_tui.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate").

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

`read.bytes` (≤ `maxPasteboardImageBytes` = 10 MB) stays referenced by the dedupe state even after a submit consumes the attachments, and is never cleared — the memory is retained until the *next* image attach. Two cheap options:

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```

  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)

Probably -1 or 0 in the constructor. `nowFn().ms - _pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs < 500` — at t=0 with initial 0: `0 - 0 = 0 < 500` → in flight! If the field defaults to 0 and the session starts at epoch ms (~1.7e12), fine. But tests use tiny times like t=1000! `DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(1000)` → 1000. If initial stamp is 0: at t=1000, `1000 - 0 = 1000 ≥ 500` → not in flight. OK. But what if initial is -1? `1000 - (-1) = 1001 ≥ 500` → fine. Need to check the field declaration.

**Behavior analysis — the deliberate-second-paste trade-off**: gesture window suppresses ANY probe within 500ms of a previous one, regardless of whether the first probe's result landed and attached. Sequence:
1. User pastes image A (empty bracketed paste) at t=0 → probe fired, stamp=0. Result lands t=50 → chip 1.
2. User copies image B, pastes at t=300 → `_pasteboardProbeInFlight()` → 300-0=300 < 500 → suppressed → NO probe → no chip for B. Text (if any) still inserts.
Is this a regression vs old behavior? Old: probe fired, read B, bytes differ from A → chip 2 attached. So a deliberate quick second image paste within 500ms now silently drops the image. 500ms double-paste: humans pressing ctrl+v twice take ~300-500ms minimum between presses — plausible! E.g., user wants the image twice. But how common is pasting the same/different image twice within half a second? Rare. And the chip count would go 1 instead of 2. The author consciously adopted this trade-off (documented in the const doc: "one gesture is one subprocess read"). It's a heuristic; acceptable. The "gesture" concept breaks when the user pastes at t=400: first chip attached at t=50; user pastes again at t=400 → suppressed. Window expiry at t=500. - **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)

dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!

```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1069
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1069
- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +291
- **Deletions**: -41
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T22:54:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart` reaches 2817 lines against the repo-enforced 2800-line gate (CI "File size guard" + `ci_fast_gate.sh`), verified locally — CI will fail. One important issue: the 500 ms result-level dedupe can still stack two chips for one user paste when probe results land >500 ms apart or the clipboard changes mid-gesture.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — fa_tui.dart 2817 > 2800 lines (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `AGENTS.md`); compact the dedupe state (declare its class in the `fa_tui_paste.dart` part file) or extract a block into a part.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — dedupe window measured from first attach + identical-bytes requirement leaves two races that reproduce the exact double-chip bug; consider gesture-level probe pairing.
- 💡 4 suggestions: untested silent `pasteImageError` branch (plus silence UX on empty pastes), 10 MB dedupe-state retention after submit, `readClipboardImage!` contract instead of a structural parameter, one subprocess spawn per bracketed-paste chunk.

**Verified locally**: all 14 paste-flow tests + 6 paste-regression tests + 138 TUI regression tests pass; text insertion, prompt-mode exclusion (AC4), and Ctrl+V behavior are correctly preserved; no new IO seams; `PasteboardResultMsg` change is source-compatible.

**Next Steps**:
1. Reclaim ≥17 lines in `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart` so the size gate passes.
2. Anchor the dedupe window to the paste gesture (or pair probes per gesture) instead of first-attach + byte identity.
3. Add one test pinning the silent over-cap/non-image bracketed-paste path.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI file-size gate will fail — `fa_tui.dart` is now 2817 lines (limit 2800)**

`AGENTS.md` ("Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file"), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)", `exit 1` on violation) and `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` (`MAX_LINES=2800`) all enforce this. `origin/main` sits at **exactly 2800**; this PR adds 17 net lines → **2817**. Verified locally with the exact CI command:

```
$ find lib test example -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ... 
lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart: 2817 lines   # → CI exits 1
```

The `fa_tui_paste.dart` header itself documents the gate ("split out of `fa_tui.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate").

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the silent `pasteImageError` branch is untested, and total silence on an image-paste gesture is questionable UX**

This `silentFailure` early-return for *image bytes that fail validation* (oversized > 10 MB, or unrecognized magic) is the only silent-failure branch with no test — the new suite only covers `PasteboardUnavailable`. One test pins the invariant end-to-end:

```dart
test('an oversized clipboard image on a bracketed paste stays silent', () async {
  var model = build(
    reader: () async => PasteboardImage(List.filled(maxPasteImageBytes + 1, 0)),
    inputText: '',
  );
  final (next, cmd) = model.update(PasteMsg(''));
  model = next as FaTuiModel;
  final followUp = await cmd?.call();
  model = model.update(followUp!).$1 as FaTuiModel;
  expect(model.attachments, isEmpty);
  expect(model.outputLines, isEmpty); // silent, per the issue invariant
});
```

Related UX consideration: an **empty** bracketed paste is the terminal's image-paste gesture — the user clearly tried to paste something. When that image is over the cap, Ctrl+V names the failure ("clipboard image too large … downscale") but menu-Paste/Cmd+V gives *zero* feedback, indistinguishable from a dead key. Consider naming the failure only when `msg.content` was empty (clear image intent), keeping text pastes fully silent as AC requires.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

`read.bytes` (≤ `maxPasteboardImageBytes` = 10 MB) stays referenced by the dedupe state even after a submit consumes the attachments, and is never cleared — the memory is retained until the *next* image attach. Two cheap options:

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: make the "reader wired" contract structural instead of a `!`**

- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +196
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

  "key": "pr-1069",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)",
    "description": "Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```"
  }
}

Key review considerations so far:

   - Performance: spawning a subprocess per paste. This is presumably the existing cost for ctrl+v. Now every bracketed paste (including large multi-chunk pastes) triggers it. Terminal apps often deliver a large paste as a SINGLE PasteMsg, but some deliver multiple. Actually — dart_tui's bracketed paste decoder produces one PasteMsg per paste, I believe. But what about a big text paste that arrives in chunks (e.g. some terminals split large pastes into multiple bracketed paste sequences)? Each would fire a probe → multiple subprocess spawns. Minor perf consideration.
   
2. **Dedupe design concerns**:
   - Dedupe is based on identical bytes within 500ms window. But a *legitimate* scenario: user copies image A, pastes (attaches chip 1), copies image A again (same content!), pastes within 500ms — second attach suppressed. Rare and acceptable, arguably intended.
   - More important: the dedupe compares ONLY against the last attached image bytes. Sequence: ctrl+v fires probe → result lands → attaches chip with bytes A at t=0. Bracketed paste probe result lands at t=100 with bytes A → suppressed. Good.
   - BUT: what about two SEPARATE bracketed pastes of the same image within 500ms? E.g., a user double-pastes quickly (paste, paste) — the second identical image within 500ms is suppressed. The user deliberately pasted twice, expecting two chips. Edge case; 500ms is small. Acceptable trade-off, but worth noting.
   - Conversely: what if the two probes of ONE user action return at times > 500ms apart? E.g., the clipboard read is slow (spawning osascript can take >500ms on a slow Mac, especially first call). Then BOTH probes attach → double chip, the exact bug this PR fixes. The window is a heuristic; races beyond 500ms reintroduce the bug. Also the reverse: the fix only dedupes if both probes see the SAME bytes. Race: user pastes image A (ctrl+v probe starts), then quickly copies image B, then the bracketed paste probe reads B → not identical → two chips (A and B) attached for one user action. Actually wait — in that scenario the clipboard really did change mid-flight, so attaching both is questionable but arguably matches "clipboard state at read time". Edge-case.
   - **No dedupe on silent bracketed-paste-only path**: In terminals that deliver ONLY bracketed paste (no key event), there's no double probe. Dedupe harmless.
   
3. **`_lastPasteboardImageBytes` holds full image bytes indefinitely** — a memory retention concern: after attaching, the model keeps a full copy of the last image bytes forever (beyond the attachments list which already holds it — actually `read.bytes` is the SAME list instance stored in the attachment, so no extra copy: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes = read.bytes` references the same List<int> as the attachment's bytes. So no additional memory beyond what the attachment already holds. OK — actually that's fine. But when the attachment is later cleared (after submit), `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` still references the bytes → retains a full image in memory after submit until the next image attach. Minor memory retention: keeps one image alive. Worth a SUGGESTION: clear `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` on submit or use a weak approach. Minor.

4. **Mutating `next` after `copyWith`** — `next._lastPasteboardImageBytes = read.bytes;` mutates the copy after creation. This follows the existing pattern (`copy._promptCompleter = ...` etc. in copyWith; and other places?). Let me check if there are other places that mutate fields post-copyWith... The `_handleThemeChanged` does `copy._wrapCache = ...; copy._stickyFmtSource = null;`. So there's precedent. OK.

Called from `_handlePaste` guarded by `== null ? null : ...` and from `_handlePasteImageKey` guarded by an early return. Safe but the `!` is a latent footgun if future callers don't guard. The doc comment says "Requires ... wired". Acceptable; could be a SUGGESTION to take the reader as a param instead: `_pasteboardProbe(reader, silentFailure)`. That would eliminate the `!`.

6. **Prompt-mode check duplication**: `_handlePaste` returns before probe when `prompt != null` — good, AC4 covered by tests.

7. **`_bytesEqual`** — O(n) byte compare on potentially multi-MB images. Two probes → one comparison of up to the image-cap bytes. What's the cap? Check `paste_image.dart` for the cap (probably a few MB). One byte-compare of ≤cap bytes is negligible. Using `ListEquality` would be idiomatic. Let me check imports of fa_tui.dart.

`AGENTS.md` ("Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file"), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)", `exit 1` on violation) and `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` (`MAX_LINES=2800`) all enforce this. `origin/main` sits at **exactly 2800**; this PR adds 17 net lines → **2817**. lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart: 2817 lines   # → CI exits 1
```

The `fa_tui_paste.dart` header itself documents the gate ("split out of `fa_tui.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate").

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

`read.bytes` (≤ `maxPasteboardImageBytes` = 10 MB) stays referenced by the dedupe state even after a submit consumes the attachments, and is never cleared — the memory is retained until the *next* image attach. Two cheap options:

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).

- **State**: open

- **Deletions**: -12

- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:11:59Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1069
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1069
- **Title**: feat(#1067): auto-detect clipboard images on any paste action (bracketed paste)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1067` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +291
- **Deletions**: -41
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T09:39:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T22:54:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).

## Test evidence
```
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart          → +14: All tests passed!
  (7 pre-existing ctrl+v regression tests + 7 new:)
  - an empty bracketed paste with a clipboard image attaches a chip   (AC1)
  - a text bracketed paste inserts the text AND attaches the image    (AC2)
  - a bracketed paste without an image stays silent — no chip, no note
  - a bracketed paste without a wired reader inserts text, no probe
  - prompt mode never probes — pastes stay plain text                 (AC4)
  - ctrl+v and the bracketed paste of one action attach ONE chip      (dedupe)
  - the same image after the dedupe window attaches again             (window expiry)
dart test test/cli/paste_regression_test.dart test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_chip_reservation_test.dart → All passed
dart test test/cli/fa_tui_double_press_test.dart test/cli/fa_tui_test.dart test/cli/tui_replay_test.dart → +138: All tests passed!
dart analyze lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart lib/src/cli/fa_tui_paste.dart test/cli/fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart → 1 pre-existing info (unnecessary_import at fa_tui.dart:13, present on clean main)
```

Fix options:
- The dedupe state is two mutable fields + two `copyWith` lines. Since `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a `part of` the same library, declare a tiny `final class PasteboardDedupeState { List<int>? bytes; int atMs; }` **in the part file** and keep a single `_pasteboardDedupe` field in the model (1 field line + 1 `copyWith` line) — reclaims ~6 lines.
- Fold the two `copy._lastPasteboard...` assignments into one line each (no doc loss) or reclaim the rest by extracting another cohesive block (e.g. a key cluster) from `fa_tui.dart` into an existing part file.

Either way, the gate must pass before merge — `Quality gate` will be red as-is.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the dedupe heuristic still lets one user action stack two chips**

The window is measured from the **first attach** (`_lastPasteboardImageAtMs`) and requires **identical bytes**. Two residual holes reintroduce the exact bug this PR fixes:

1. **Skewed land times.** Both probes are concurrent subprocess reads (`osascript`/`xclip`/`wl-paste`/PowerShell). If one read stalls >500 ms relative to the other (PowerShell cold start, macOS TCC permission dialog on first `osascript` use, loaded box), the second result lands *outside* the window → both attach.
2. **Clipboard changes mid-gesture.** Probe 1 reads image A; the user copies image B before probe 2 lands (inside the window but with different bytes) → `_bytesEqual` fails → both attach.

Consider gesture-level pairing instead of result-level dedupe: when `_handlePasteImageKey` fires its probe, stamp a paste-gesture time on the model; `_handlePaste` (and vice versa) skips its own probe when a gesture probe is already in flight within the window. That closes both holes and halves the subprocess spawns. At minimum, anchor the window to the *gesture's first probe* rather than to the first successful attach, and document the residual races in the `[_pasteboardDedupeWindowMs]` doc.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the silent `pasteImageError` branch is untested, and total silence on an image-paste gesture is questionable UX**

This `silentFailure` early-return for *image bytes that fail validation* (oversized > 10 MB, or unrecognized magic) is the only silent-failure branch with no test — the new suite only covers `PasteboardUnavailable`. One test pins the invariant end-to-end:

```dart
test('an oversized clipboard image on a bracketed paste stays silent', () async {
  var model = build(
    reader: () async => PasteboardImage(List.filled(maxPasteImageBytes + 1, 0)),
    inputText: '',
  );
  final (next, cmd) = model.update(PasteMsg(''));
  model = next as FaTuiModel;
  final followUp = await cmd?.call();
  model = model.update(followUp!).$1 as FaTuiModel;
  expect(model.attachments, isEmpty);
  expect(model.outputLines, isEmpty); // silent, per the issue invariant
});
```

Related UX consideration: an **empty** bracketed paste is the terminal's image-paste gesture — the user clearly tried to paste something. When that image is over the cap, Ctrl+V names the failure ("clipboard image too large … downscale") but menu-Paste/Cmd+V gives *zero* feedback, indistinguishable from a dead key. Consider naming the failure only when `msg.content` was empty (clear image intent), keeping text pastes fully silent as AC requires.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` pins up to 10 MB for the rest of the session**

- Clear the state wherever the chips are consumed on submit (`attachments: const []` path).
- Or store a fingerprint instead of the bytes (length + FNV-1a over the first/last N bytes): makes the state O(1) and `_bytesEqual` a trivial comparison. Collision risk is negligible for the 500 ms same-gesture window this protects.

Not urgent (bounded to one image), but free to fix while the state object is being reshaped for the size gate.

blocks.text:
The reworked implementation. Now let me analyze it carefully:

**Claim 1 — Size gate**: fa_tui.dart = 2774 lines ✅ (2800 gate). fa_tui_paste.dart = 165. Need to verify no other file violates (run the CI find command).

**Claim 2 — Gesture pairing**: `_firePasteboardProbe` — checks `_pasteboardProbeInFlight()`; if in flight → `(this, null)` — no probe. Otherwise stamps `armed._pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs = now` and returns the probe cmd.

Wait — there's a subtle issue with `_handlePaste`:
```dart
final (armed, probe) = _firePasteboardProbe(reader, silentFailure: content.isNotEmpty);
return (armed.copyWith(editor: editor.insert(content)), probe);
```
The stamp is set on `armed` via `copyWith()` then `armed._pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs = ...`. Then `armed.copyWith(editor: ...)` — does copyWith preserve `_pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs`? copyWith copies private fields (`copy._lastPasteboardImageBytes` was previously copied; now presumably `copy._pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs = _pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs;`). Need to verify in fa_tui.dart copyWith.

**Critical correctness question for the stamp design**: `_pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs` — what's the initial value? Probably -1 or 0 in the constructor. `nowFn().ms - _pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs < 500` — at t=0 with initial 0: `0 - 0 = 0 < 500` → in flight! If the field defaults to 0 and the session starts at epoch ms (~1.7e12), fine. But tests use tiny times like t=1000! `DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(1000)` → 1000. If initial stamp is 0: at t=1000, `1000 - 0 = 1000 ≥ 500` → not in flight. OK. But what if initial is -1? `1000 - (-1) = 1001 ≥ 500` → fine. Need to check the field declaration.

**Behavior analysis — the deliberate-second-paste trade-off**: gesture window suppresses ANY probe within 500ms of a previous one, regardless of whether the first probe's result landed and attached. Sequence:
1. User pastes image A (empty bracketed paste) at t=0 → probe fired, stamp=0. Result lands t=50 → chip 1.
2. User copies image B, pastes at t=300 → `_pasteboardProbeInFlight()` → 300-0=300 < 500 → suppressed → NO probe → no chip for B. Text (if any) still inserts.
Is this a regression vs old behavior? Old: probe fired, read B, bytes differ from A → chip 2 attached. So a deliberate quick second image paste within 500ms now silently drops the image. 500ms double-paste: humans pressing ctrl+v twice take ~300-500ms minimum between presses — plausible! E.g., user wants the image twice. But how common is pasting the same/different image twice within half a second? Rare. And the chip count would go 1 instead of 2. The author consciously adopted this trade-off (documented in the const doc: "one gesture is one subprocess read"). It's a heuristic; acceptable. I might note it as residual behavior, SUGGESTION-level at most. Hmm — but wait, there's an asymmetry: the window is anchored at probe FIRE time, and the result may take 300ms to land. The "gesture" concept breaks when the user pastes at t=400: first chip attached at t=50; user pastes again at t=400 → suppressed. Window expiry at t=500. So the effective minimum spacing between attachable image pastes is ~500ms — fine.

But there's a subtler issue: **the stamp is on the model state returned by the handler — does it survive?** In `_handlePaste`, `armed.copyWith(editor: ...)` — copyWith carries private fields if implemented. Verify.

Also in `_handlePasteImageKey`: `return _firePasteboardProbe(reader, silentFailure: false);` — returns `(FaTuiModel, Cmd?)` where the declared return type is `(Model, Cmd?)?` — `FaTuiModel` is a `Model`, and Dart records are covariant in their type args? Record types `(FaTuiModel, Cmd?)` is a subtype of `(Model, Cmd?)` — yes, records are covariant. OK.

**Interaction with ctrl+c window wrapper**: `_handleTerminalMsg` wraps `_handlePaste` in `_withFreshCtrlCWindow(msg, () => _handlePaste(msg))`. The wrapper takes the returned model and possibly adjusts ctrlC state. Does `_withFreshCtrlCWindow` build its own copy via the handler's returned model? It returns `(model, cmd)` from the callback presumably with adjustments. The armed stamp travels in the returned model. Need a quick look to confirm nothing rebuilds from `this`.

**Potential new bug — `_firePasteboardProbe` returns `(this, null)` when in flight, then `_handlePaste` does `armed.copyWith(editor: ...)`**: in that case armed == this (no stamp), then copyWith(editor) → normal insert. Good.

**Prompt-mode**: unchanged, returns before reader check. ✅ AC4.

**silentFailure: content.isNotEmpty**: empty paste → false → names failure. Text paste → true → silent. ✅ matches discussion.

**Claim 5 — structural reader param**: `_pasteboardProbe(reader, {required silentFailure})` — no `!` anywhere. ✅

**Claim 4 — memory**: `_lastPasteboardImageBytes` deleted → single int stamp. ✅

**Claim 6 — rate limit**: window doubles as rate limit: max one subprocess per 500ms across both paths. ✅ (trade-off noted above).

Now things to verify:
1. `_pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs` field declaration + copyWith propagation in fa_tui.dart.
2. The moved `_handlePaste`/`_fixPasteMojibake` — call sites in fa_tui.dart: `update()` still routes PasteMsg → `_handleTerminalMsg` → `_withFreshCtrlCWindow(msg, () => _handlePaste(msg))`. Since `_handlePaste` is now an extension method, unqualified call from instance method resolves via the in-scope extension (same library). Verify it compiles — run analyze + tests.
3. Wait — extension methods can't access `super`, but can access `this` members. `_handlePaste` uses `prompt`, `_promptCompleter`, `copyWith`, `editor`, `callbacks` — all public or library-private members of FaTuiModel — accessible from the extension (same library via part). ✅
4. `static String _fixPasteMojibake` inside extension — static methods in extensions are allowed (called as `FaTuiPaste._fixPasteMojibake` or unqualified within the extension). It's used within `_handlePaste` in the same extension. ✅. But was `_fixPasteMojibake` referenced elsewhere in fa_tui.dart (tests?)? Check.
5. Size gate across lib test example bin.
6. Run all test suites.
7. New tests in the test file — read the updated test file (189 additions).
8. The doc comment on PasteboardResultMsg now says "only Ctrl+V and image-intent pastes (empty payload) name their failures" ✅.

Edge: `_pasteboardProbeInFlight` uses `nowFn()` — fine.

One more check — **the `_withFreshCtrlCWindow` wrapper**: it may CONSTRUCT a new model from the returned one? Let me re-check that function. Also whether `update()`'s heartbeat wrapper (`copyWith(busyLastEventMs: ...)`) preserves the stamp (copyWith must carry it).

Also potential issue: **`_firePasteboardProbe` stamps `armed` but `_handlePasteImageKey` previously returned `(this, cmd)` — now returns armed (a new model state with bumped frameNonce)**. Any behavioral consequence? copyWith bumps frameNonce → repaint. Harmless.

And: the stamp is set even if the probe result later FAILS (e.g., PasteboardUnavailable). The window still blocks re-probes for 500ms. Fine.

**Skewed-land-time hole closed?** Old hole: two concurrent reads, second lands >500ms after first attach → double chip. New: only ONE read exists per gesture → structurally impossible. ✅ Author's claim verified by design.

**Mid-gesture clipboard change hole?** No second read → no comparison → impossible. ✅

Now the remaining NEW review angles for this round:
- New trade-off: deliberate second paste within 500ms silently drops the image (no chip, no feedback for TEXT pastes since silent; for empty pastes — wait, empty paste within window → suppressed at source → no failure named either. E.g., user pastes image (attaches), then 300ms later pastes again (empty) → nothing happens at all. Rare; acceptable but worth one line? Maybe fold into a suggestion to document. Actually the const doc already documents "tmux/screen split large pastes into adjacent blocks" absorption. The deliberate-double-paste case is inherent to any gesture window. I'll note it in the general comment as a known trade-off, not a new thread. Hmm — guidelines say surface maximum findings; but this is a documented, deliberate design trade-off of the approach I myself recommended. A suggestion-level not…

The handler runs on `self`; armed stamp set on handler's returned copy. Fine.

c) **What about TWO gestures racing via different paths where the first path is the PasteMsg and second is ctrl+v?** Symmetric — both go through `_firePasteboardProbe`. ✅

d) **Test-time clock initial value**: `_pasteboardProbeFiredAtMs = -1` default. In prod, first probe at real epoch. `-1` initial: `now - (-1) = now + 1`. At session start in prod, now ≈ 1.7e12 → not in flight. In tests with t=1000 → 1001 ≥ 500 → not in flight. ✅ No false "in flight" at startup.

e) **Silent `PasteboardResultMsg` default `silentFailure = false`** — retained.

Hmm, one could argue for a shorter window (200ms) as the earlier suggestion noted. The author chose 500ms to also cover the ctrl+v twin. The ctrl+v twin arrives within ms, so 200ms would still cover twins AND tmux splits... but not slow twins (the test pins twin at t=1400 = 400ms later). tmux splits can be seconds apart for huge pastes. Trade-off is real; 500ms is a reasonable middle. I'll note it once, SUGGESTION, in the general comment — not a thread (it's the documented design).

h) **`_pasteboardProbeInFlight` uses `nowFn()` twice** (once in `_firePasteboardProbe` for the stamp, once in the check) — no issue.

## PR Description

Fixes #1067

## What
Clipboard-image attach was hardcoded to the `ctrl+v` key event in `_handlePasteImageKey`; every other paste path (terminal menu Paste, Cmd+V, Shift+Insert — all arriving as bracketed paste `PasteMsg`) never checked the clipboard. Now `_handlePaste` fires the **same** pasteboard probe additively:

- **Text insertion unchanged** — the probe rides along, text still lands in the editor.
- **Silent failures** — probe results carry `silentFailure`, so a plain-text paste never prints clipboard errors (issue invariant); Ctrl+V keeps naming its failures.
- **Prompt mode never probes** — pasted API keys stay plain text (AC4).
- **Dedupe** — one user action can fire both `ctrl+v` and its bracketed paste; the second identical image inside a 500ms window is suppressed instead of stacking a second chip (injectable `nowFn` clock keeps the tests deterministic).
- `_handlePasteImageKey` ctrl+v behavior untouched (regression-pinned by the 7 pre-existing tests).

No new IO, no `dart:io` in lib/ — reuses the exact `FaTuiCallbacks.readClipboardImage` seam (`osascript`/xclip/wl-paste/PowerShell via `clipboard_reader.dart`).
